title: Pub/Sub Message Broker
description: Build an in-memory pub/sub message broker with topic hierarchies, wildcard subscriptions, and at-least-once delivery.

steps.title: Create topic data structure
steps.description: Build a topic tree structure where each topic (e.g. 'sensors.temperature.room1') is a path in a tree. Create a `TopicTree` class with methods to `addTopic(path)` and `getTopic(path)`. Each node has a `name`, `children` map, and optional `subscribers` array. Build topics for 'sensors.temperature.room1', 'sensors.humidity.room1', 'actuators.light.kitchen' and print the full tree.
hints: Split topic path by '.' and walk the tree, creating nodes as needed
Use a Map or dictionary for children at each node for O(1) lookup
Print the tree recursively with indentation to show the hierarchy

verification.successMessage: Topic tree with hierarchical structure is correctly built and printed!
verification.failureMessage: Print a hierarchical tree showing sensors and actuators with their child topics.

steps.title: Implement basic publish/subscribe
steps.description: Add `subscribe(topic, callback)` and `publish(topic, message)` methods to your `Broker` class. subscribe() stores the callback under the topic node. publish() walks the tree to find the topic and calls all subscriber callbacks with the message. Subscribe to 'sensors.temperature.room1', publish a temperature reading of 22.5, and verify the callback receives it by printing the message.
hints: Store callbacks in an array on the topic node: node.subscribers.push(callback)
publish() should navigate to the topic node and iterate over subscribers
Test by subscribing with a callback that console.logs the received message

verification.successMessage: Messages published to a topic are delivered to all subscribers!
verification.failureMessage: Print 'Received: <message>' in your subscriber callback to show the message was delivered.

steps.title: Add wildcard subscriptions
steps.description: Implement two wildcard levels: `+` matches exactly one level (e.g. 'sensors.+.room1' matches 'sensors.temperature.room1'), and `#` matches one or more levels (e.g. 'sensors.#' matches 'sensors.temperature.room1' and 'sensors.humidity.room1'). Test both wildcards and print which subscriptions matched each published message.
hints: For '+': match exactly one topic level — skip comparing that level
For '#': match any remaining levels — if the pattern has # at the end, it matches everything below
Iterate all subscriptions when publishing and check each against the topic pattern

verification.successMessage: Single-level (+) and multi-level (#) wildcards match the correct topic sets!
verification.failureMessage: Show that 'sensors.+.room1' matches specific sensors and 'sensors.#' matches everything under sensors.

steps.title: Implement durable subscriptions
steps.description: Add durable subscription support with offline message storage. When a subscriber is created with `durable: true`, store messages published while the subscriber is marked as offline. Implement `disconnect()` and `reconnect()` methods. On reconnect, replay stored messages to the subscriber. Print stored messages and replay them.
hints: Store offline messages in a queue per subscriber: offlineMessages[subscriberId].push(message)
When the subscriber reconnects, iterate the offline queue and call their callback for each message
Clear the offline queue after replaying

verification.successMessage: Durable subscribers receive messages published while they were offline!
verification.failureMessage: Print 'Replaying <count> offline messages' when a durable subscriber reconnects.

steps.title: Add delivery acknowledgments
steps.description: Implement at-least-once delivery by tracking message acknowledgments. Assign each message a unique ID. After delivering to a subscriber, wait for an `ack(messageId)` call. If not acked within a configurable timeout, redeliver. Track delivery counts and print delivery statistics showing how many times each message was delivered.
hints: Assign a UUID or incrementing ID to each message
Set a timeout per subscriber — if ack not received, push the message back to the delivery queue
Track deliveryCount per messageId and print 'Message X delivered N times'

verification.successMessage: At-least-once delivery with ack tracking and redelivery works correctly!
verification.failureMessage: Print delivery stats showing how many times each message was delivered to each subscriber.

steps.title: Build a message router
steps.description: Combine everything into a complete `MessageBroker` class with stats tracking. Implement methods: `createTopic(path)`, `subscribe(pattern, callback, options)`, `publish(topic, message)`, `getStats()` returning total messages routed, active subscriptions, and delivery success rate. Publish 5 messages to various topics and print the final stats report.
hints: getStats() should return a readable object or formatted string with all metrics
Test with a mix of exact and wildcard subscriptions across multiple topics

verification.successMessage: Complete pub/sub broker with stats reporting is fully functional!
verification.failureMessage: Print a stats report showing total messages routed, active subscriptions, and delivery success rate.
